observed_title: The affine subspace concentration inequality for centered convex bodies
version: Acta Mathematica Hungarica 175 (2025), issue 1, pp. 26–36; DOI 10.1007/s10474-025-01508-4; 11 PDF pages. Supplementary downloaded version; bibliographic identity has not been independently checked beyond PDF first page and catalog Crossref record.

read_ranges.scope: entire article: cone-volume preliminaries, all lifting lemmas, affine subspace concentration proof, equality cases, proof details and references

topic_relevance.K05: irrelevant to Talagrand convex concentration: the paper proves a convex-geometric inequality for cone-volume measures and affine subspaces of centered convex bodies; it is not a probabilistic concentration inequality for Lipschitz functions under Gaussian or product measure.

definitions.name: cone-volume measure
definitions.statement: For K containing the origin in its interior, VK(ω)=n^(−1)∫_ω hK(u)dSK(u); equivalently it is the volume of the star pyramid over the regular boundary portion whose outer normals lie in ω.

definitions.name: centered convex body
definitions.statement: A convex body K⊂R^n is centered when its centroid is at the origin; the result also assumes 0 is in its interior so the polar K⋆ and cone-volume measure are defined.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 1.2 (affine subspace concentration for centered convex bodies)
assumptions: K⊂R^n is a centered convex body with the origin in its interior.
theorem_cards.statement: VK(π(bd(K⋆)∩A)) ≤ ((dim(A)+1)/(n+1)) VK(S^(n−1)). This is a geometric cone-volume inequality, not a tail probability.
proof_steps: Lift K successively to centered pyramids K^(j), preserving the relevant cone volume attached to A.
Map the affine subspace A to linear spaces L^(j) of dimension dim(A)+1 and map polar boundary normals into the corresponding lifted polar boundary.
Apply the linear subspace concentration inequality in dimension n+j, obtaining factor (dim(A)+1)/(n+j) times vol(K^(j)).
Use the pyramid volume ratio vol(K^(j))/vol(K)=(n+j+1)/(n+1), and let j→∞ to get the coefficient (dim(A)+1)/(n+1).
gaps: It concerns cone-volume measure, polarity, and centered convex geometry; no probability law, Lipschitz function, median, or product-space random vector appears.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 4.1 (two equality cases)
assumptions: K is a centered convex body.
Either A is a singleton, or A is a supporting hyperplane of K⋆ spanned by boundary points of K⋆.
theorem_cards.statement: Equality in the corresponding cone-volume concentration inequality is characterized by K being a pyramid with the stated base or apex.
proof_steps: For the singleton case, use concavity of the section function.
For the supporting-hyperplane case, express the cone-volume fraction as an affine function on K.
Apply sublevel-volume comparison to the affine function under the uniform distribution on K; equality forces the pyramid structure.
gaps: Only these two special equality configurations are characterized in the article.

constant_dependence.explicit: The coefficient (dim(A)+1)/(n+1) depends on affine-subspace dimension and ambient dimension; no probability-tail constant is present.
constant_dependence.dependence: The proof obtains the affine factor by a high-dimensional lifting limit of the linear cone-volume inequality.

endpoint_limits.scope: A result for centered convex bodies with 0 in the interior and polar boundary data; it is not a Talagrand concentration or isoperimetric tail statement.
endpoint_limits.equality: Equality is characterized only in the two special cases in Theorem 4.1.

reusable_methods.method: Pyramid lifting reduces an affine-subspace geometric statement to a linear-subspace statement in higher dimension.
reusable_methods.transfer: Only a geometric proof technique; there is no justified transfer to Gaussian/product concentration without a separate probabilistic formulation.

unchecked: All 11 extracted pages were read. Theorem 1.2 on PDF page 4 and the lifted-dimension coefficient limit on PDF page 9 were visually checked against PyMuPDF renders in reviews/HK.

The geometric proof was followed as written; cited prior linear cone-volume concentration results were not independently re-proved. This paper is preserved as an exclusion record and is not evidence for K05 Talagrand concentration.
